Yemen Civil War — Situation on the Aden Front:
Over the past few hours, Ansar Allah forces have intensified their attacks toward Aden in southwestern Yemen, following their capture of Bab al-Mandab on September 10.
Ansar Allah forces have captured and established full control over the Ras Al-Arah area and the mountains overlooking it, west of Aden.

Early this morning, clashes erupted between Iranian security forces and the People's Fighters Front, formerly known as Jaysh al-Adl, following a raid by Iranian forces on one of the group's safe houses in Saravan, Sistan and Baluchestan Province, southeastern Iran.
The clashes have been ongoing for approximately 11 hours. Pro-IRGC sources claim that weapons and fighters entered the area from outside the region.
A massive convoy of Yemeni prisoners of war made its way from Mocha to Sanaa, greeted by crowds in cities and towns along the route.
A local in Jordan recently found the infrared seeker of an MIM-401 (Talon) interceptor, used by the U.S. THAAD anti-ballistic missile (ABM) system.

Update on the Marib front:
Ansar Allah forces are continuing their assault toward Marib from the southwest, attempting to advance toward Manin Al-Ashraf while pushing north along the Marib–Ataq Highway.
West of Marib, Ansar Allah forces are pushing eastward toward the city from the Sirwah Road and the Sanaa–Marib Highway. Clashes are already taking place on the outskirts of Marib.
In the northwest, elements of the Yemeni Army's 3rd and 7th Military Regions remain present and in control of the village of Asdas. There are no reports of clashes there so far.
Based on what we have seen on other fronts, many of which are collapsing rapidly, Asdas may not hold for long if Ansar Allah continues advancing. The situation around Marib is also becoming increasingly serious, with reports that military convoys have begun preparing for an evacuation should attempts to push Ansar Allah back fail.
